Reference: Stebbing SA (1876) Catalogue of Amphipodous Crustacea in the British Museum. British Museum, London. (BHL: https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/6466)

Diagnosis: Body elongated, laterally compressed, abdominal segments 1–3 fused; head slightly shorter than pereonites 1 and 2 combined; antenna 1 longer than antenna 2; gnathopod 1 propodus with elongated palm; gnathopod 2 propodus with obtuse posterior distal process, resembling the sharp distal projection; pereopods 5 and 6 dactylus bifurcated; pereopod 7 basis elongated; telson each lobe terminated as rounded digitate. (abstract, ZSE 2023)
Remarks: Cerapus rivulus sp. nov. resembles C. bundegi Lowry & Berents, 1996, C. herdmani Walker, 1904 and C. tunnidonkawa Pramok & Wongkamhaeng, 2017, but is mainly distinguished by having pereopods 5 and 6 dactylus bifurcated, strongly obtuse posterior distal process of the gnathopod 2 propodus, and pereopod 7 basis elongated and wide.
Reference: Katnoum W, Saetung P, Keetapithchayakul S, Rahim AA, Wongkamhaeng K (2023) ZSE 99(2): 557–574. https://doi.org/10.3897/zse.99.107974
WoRMs: — (ยังไม่ถูกบันทึกในฐานข้อมูล)

Description: Antenna 2, fourth joint more than twice as long as the third with lower margin produced distally into a strong forward-curving tooth below and a small tooth above; and a low narrow tooth or ridge at the lower inside surface at the proximal end; Gnathopod 2 fourth joint fringed with customary double row of extremely long setae and seventh joint with three broad teeth. The peduncle of uropod 1 has a pointed triangular cone at its distal end; Telson triangular, with obtusely pointed apex. (Nayar, 1950)
Remarks: Nayar (1950) described Chelicorophium madrasensis from the Madras Coast, India, which is characterized by antenna 2 article 4 inner surface with 2 proximal spines and epimeron 1 smooth and naked. The specimens from the current study are similar to those of Nayar, but the telson is truncated, whereas it is pointed in Chelicorophium madrasensis. (Wongkamhaeng et al. 2015, ZooKeys 505)
Reference: Nayar KN (1959) Bull. Madras Govt. Mus. VI(3). | Redescription: Wongkamhaeng K, Nabhitabhata J, Towatana P (2015) ZooKeys 505: 35–50. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.505.9751

Diagnosis: Specific Diagnosis: In general shape of the body, antennæ, peraeopods, etc. resembling G. megnae, but differing markedly in the gnathopods. In the male the first gnathopod is complexly subchelate, having the carpus greatly dilated; the basal joint is broad but not specially dilated, the ischium and merus are short, the latter bearing on its hind margin a fringe of long plumose setæ; the carpus is very large, oval, but having the postero-distal angle produced into a sharp tooth; on the palm between this tooth and the base of the propod is a triangular projection; the hind margin of the carpus bears a very distinct fringe of long plumose setæ and there is another slightly oblique row on the surface of the joint; the propod is narrow at the base, widening slightly distally and bears an oblique row of long plumose setæ; the finger is strong, slightly curved and, with the propod, can be bent over to meet the distal tooth of the carpus. In the female the first gnathopod is of more normal shape and scarcely subchelate, the carpus is broader than the propod but not produced into a distal tooth, the propod is oblong about as long as the carpus; the four distal joints bear numerous long plumose setæ. The second gnathopod in both sexes is somewhat similar to the first gnathopod of the female but more slender and has the merus produced distally into a lobe or scoop. The third uropod has only one branch as in G. megnae but in old specimens this branch becomes somewhat more elongated than in that species. Colour light yellow with dark patches or reticulate markings, particularly on the dorsal surface. Length of body, about 7 mm.  (Chilton 1921: 552–554) I Diagnosis: Male gnathopod 1 ischium and merus lacking posterodistal projection; merus to propodus heavily setose posteromedially; carpus with 2 posterodistal teeth; propodus straight. Male gnathopod 2, coxa without posteromedial projection; basis straight; merus divergent posteriorly, posterodistal margin with many long setae; carpus and propodus same in size, elongate, heavily setose posteromedially, propodus posterodistal corner with 2 short robust setae; dactylus very short. Uropod 1 with an inter-ramal process. (Thacker et al. 2025, Zootaxa 5716(4): 476–477)
Reference: Chilton C (1921) Mem. Indian Mus. 5(8): 519–558. https://archive.org/details/memoirsofindianm57111indi | Thacker DR, Patro S, Bhoi G, Myers AA, Kumar RK, Trivedi JN (2025) Zootaxa 5716(4): 451–482.

Diagnosis: Male pereon without ventral processes. Male gnathopod 1 carpus and propodus subequal, posterior margin with single tooth and hook shape uropod 3 rami. (Thacker et al. 2025, Zootaxa 5716(4): 477)
Remarks: Barnard (1935) described this species on the basis of specimens collected from Vembanad Lake and Mundattalkari, Kerala, India (Thacker et al. 2025)

Diagnosis: Body: slightly cylindrical; urosomite segments separate, with no dorsal depression; no elongation of urosomite 1. Mature males possessing a medioventral spine on first pereonite. Head: one-fourth longer than pereonite 1, cuboidal; lateral lobes rounded, projecting slightly beyond a short acute rostrum. Eyes large and dark. Antenna 1: greater than one-half body length, with 20 articles total; flagellum with 17 articles. Accessory flagellum consisting of one minute article with short distal hairs. Article 1 of peduncle with ventral spines. Antenna 2: from three-fourths length to longer than antenna 1; article 2 barely visible from lateral view; spines on articles 3, 4, and 5; male antenna stout. Mouthparts: form subquadrate bundle. Mandible with large trit erative molar; incisors and lacinia mobilis toothed. Mandibular palp tri-articulate, article 2 longest, article 3 slightly longer than article 1, setation heaviest medio-distally on article 3. Maxillipeds: generalized, inner plates of normal size, with distal setation; outer plates twice the length of inner plates with heaviest setation on medial sides. Maxilliped palp, four-articulate; article 2 twice length of articles 1 and 3; terminal palp claw-like; when extended, palp twice length of outer plate. Male gnathopod 1: massive, carpochelate; articles 2 and 5 greatly enlarged; article 2, length one and one half times width, broad and ovate, subequal in length to article 5, medial side concave, anterior edge sharp; article 3 small; article 4 elongate; article 5 length twice its width with three distal posterior teeth, one tooth enlarged, forming a thumb, anterior edge with short transverse grooves and four anterior spines; article 6 subquadrangular, one-third length of article 5. Female gnathopod 1: reduced, articles 4 and 5 possessing posterior hairs with pinnate barbs; article 6 with three posterior spines; article 7, serrated claw forming acute angle with article 6. Male gnathopod 2: subchelate, smaller than gnathopod 1, article 2 twice length of article 5; articles 4, 5, and 6 possessing posterior hairs with pinnate barbs, serrated subchelate claw forms transverse angle with article 6: sexual dimorphism apparent, male with elongate article 2. Pereopods 1-5 as described by Stephensen, 1938 (as pereiopods 3-7), coxae reduced, 1-4 subquadrate. Female gnathopod 2: similar to male gnathopod 2 but with shortened article 2. Uropod 1 and 2 biramous; uropod 3 uniramous; numerous spines on all uropods; uropod 1 projecting posteriorly slightly beyond uropod 2 and 3, prominent distal peduncular process on uropod 1, urosomite 1 with two spines on antero-lateral surface. Telson small, button-like, with pronounced medial groove. Largest male examined 22 mm in length, largest female 13 mm; cuticle mottled gray to gray brown. (Chapman & Dorman 1975: 106)
Reference: Chapman JW, Dorman JA (1975) Bull. So. Calif. Acad. Sci. 74(2): 104–108. | Original: Stephensen K (1938) Annotationes Zoologicae Japonenses 17: 255–262.

Diagnosis: Adult male antenna 2 with an ovoid lamellate appendix situated mediodistally on peduncular article 2. Male gnathopod 2 with an enlarged propodus bearing a long, acute posteroproximal process; dactylus elongate and strongly curved posteriorly. The antennal appendix is the decisive character: the authors state that it is absent from all other Kamaka species known to them at publication. The appendix is absent in the female and smaller in the 1.7-mm male paratype than in the 2.1-mm holotype. Its size is therefore growth-dependent, and absence alone must not be used to exclude females from this species.
Description: Body surface smooth, cuticle polished. Eyes medium-sized. Antenna 1 with ratio of lengths of peduncular articles 1–3 1:1.5:0.9; flagellum with 10 articles. Antenna 2 with distinct swelled article 4; flagellum with 1 long, 5 medium-sized and 1 tiny distal article, article 1 excavate posteriorly, with serrate posterior margins, tip of article 5 with several setae. (Ariyama, Siriamornpun & Gobin, 2010) Female, based on the 1.7-mm allotype, OMNH-Ar-7751: antenna 2 more slender and without the lamellate appendix; gnathopod 1 coxa smaller than in the male; gnathopod 2 subchelate, with an oblique palm defined by a small robust seta.
Remarks:
This new species resembles Kamaka koreana in the possession of a 1-articulate flagellum of antenna 2 [p. 57]. It can, however, be distinguished from the latter by the excavation of the posterior margin of the second peduncular article of antenna 2, and the posteroventral spine on each side of the pleonites 2 and 3 in the male. The ovoid lamellate appendix on male antenna 2, peduncular article 2, is the explicitly stated distinctive feature.
Male gnathopod 2 resembles that of K. biwae and K. morinoi; its general shape alone is therefore insufficient for separation.
In the smaller male paratype, the appendix is smaller, and the propodus, posterior process and dactylus of gnathopod 2 are shorter than in the holotype.
The paper records the species from Outer and Middle Songkhla Lagoon. The holotype was collected from brown soft clay at 1.2 m depth and salinity 30 psu.
Reference: Ariyama H, Siriamornpun S, Gobin J (2010) Zootaxa 2404: 57–62.

Diagnosis: Adult male antenna 2 with distinctly swollen peduncular article 4, lacking a distal spine. Male gnathopod 2 with a broad propodus, a convex distal margin and an acute posteroproximal process; anterior margin without a blunt triangular process. Male coxa 1 with a right-angled posteroventral corner. This combination separates the species from the morphologically similar K. poppi and K. taditadi in the authors’ comparisons.
Description: Body slender, smooth. Eyes medium-sized. Antenna 1 with ratio of lengths of peduncular articles 1–3 1:1.2:0.9, peduncular article 1 with 2 penicillate setae at ventrodistal corner; flagellum with 9 medium-sized articles, articles 7–9 each with aesthetasc at ventrodistal corner. Antenna 2 with distinct swelled article 4, ratio of lengths of peduncular articles 3–5 1:2.6:1.7; flagellum with 1 long, 4 medium-sized and 1 tiny distal article, article 1 excavate posteriorly, with serrate posterior margins, tip of article 5 with several setae. Female, based on the 2.4-mm allotype, OMNH-Ar-7755: antenna 2 peduncular article 4 slender, flagellar article 1 without the posterior excavation; coxa 1 smaller than in the male, with rounded posteroventral corner; gnathopod 2 with oblique palm defined by a small robust seta.
Remarks: This new species is characterized by the swelled peduncular article 4 of antenna 2 and the wide propodus of gnathopod 2 in adult male, and shares these characters with Kamaka poppi and K. taditadi. However, K. poppi has the following characters (Bamber, 2003): (1) peduncular article 4 of male antenna 2 with distal spine (absent in K. songkhlaensis), (2) merus of male gnathopod 2 long (relatively short in K. songkhlaensis), (3) distal margin of propodus of male gnathopod 2 almost straight (convex in K. songkhlaensis), (4) carpi of male pereopods 3, 4 short (relatively long in K. songkhlaensis), (5) inner rami of uropods 1, 2 without marginal spine (present in K. songkhlaensis). On the other hand, K. taditadi has the following characters (Thomas & Barnard, 1991; Krapp-Schickel & Myers, 2006): (1) posteroventral corner of male coxa 1 round (right-angled in K. songkhlaensis), (2) merus and carpus of male gnathopod 2 long (relatively short in K. songkhlaensis), (3) anterior margin of propodus of male gnathopod 2 with blunt triangular process (absent in K. songkhlaensis). In addition, the new species inhabits brackish environment, whereas K. taditadi is a marine species.
Reference: Ariyama H, Siriamornpun S, Gobin J (2010) Zootaxa 2404: 62–67.

Description: Head: lateral cephalic lobes subround, with notch, forming accessory lobes ventrally. Antenna 1: accessory flagellum (with 25-27 articles of main flagellum) consists of three articles. Antenna 2: flagellum densely setose.
Remarks: This new species is characterized by having setae densely on the flagellum of antenna 2. This new species is different from M. nitida in the presence of the notch at the inferior antennal corner of the head. This new species differs from the four species [M. rylovae, M. koreana, M. nagatai, M. bingoensis] in the ovoid article 6 of male gnathopod 2, in the less developed posterodistal lobe of article 2 of pereopods 5–7, in the shapes of articles 6 and 7 of male gnathopod 1, and in the female coxa 6 bearing a row of denticles.
Reference: Yamato S (1988) PSMBL 33(1/3): 79–95. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176148
Hirayama A (1992) Oedicerotid amphipods from Hong Kong. Asian Marine Biology 9: 139–166.

Diagnosis: Body long and narrow, side plates small, much shallower than the segments. Pleon segment 3 with the postero-lateral angle quadrate. Eyes small, irregular, apparently imperfect. Upper antenna about three-fourths the length of body, first and second joints of peduncle subequal, elongate; third short, flagellum slender, longer than peduncle, accessory flagellum of two slender joints. Lower antenna a little longer than peduncle of upper, last two joints of peduncle subequal, flagellum shorter than last joint, consisting of one long joint followed by two or three indistinct ones. First gnathopod with the merus produced posteriorly into a rounded lobe, carpus much longer than the propod, with numerous tufts of setules on the posterior margin and on the surface near to it; propod widening distally, palm neatly transverse, evenly convex. Second gnathopod much larger than the first, carpus short, about one-third the length of the propod; propod irregularly oval, palm oblique, sinuous, about equal in length to the hind margin; finger strongly curved, bulging on the inner margin near its base. Third, fourth and fifth peraeopods increasing in size posteriorly, basal joint in the third narrow, slightly wider in the fourth and greatly widened and enlarged in the fifth, its posterior margin irregularly serrate, most distinctly so in the fifth peraeopod; in the fifth peraeopod the merus is dilated posteriorly. Third uropods greatly elongating, peduncle longer than the telson, outer branch formed of two subequal joints, somewhat broadened, inner branch small, tapering, tipped with one or two setae. Telson cleft to the base, each lobe narrowing posteriorly and bearing a stout setule at the extremity. Colour (in spirit), whitish. Length of body, about 10 mm. (Chilton 1921: 532–533)
Reference: Chilton C (1921) Mem. Indian Mus. 5(8): 519–558. https://archive.org/details/memoirsofindianm57111indi

Diagnosis: Antenna 1 accessory flagellum long, with 9-10 articles. Mandibular palp with 2 apical setae. Gnathopod 2 palm subacute, two thirds length of propodus posterior margin, subrectangular distomedial shelf with robust setae, midpalm dominated by expanded cuticle covered in fine setae, palmar margin defined by rounded corner with 2 robust setae; dactylus without posteroproximal shelf, closing along and equal to length of palm. Pereonite 7 without carina. Pleonites 1-3 bicarinate. Epimeron 1-2 posterodistal corner with 3 serrate teeth. Epimeron 3 ventral margin serrate, posterodistal corner with 2 teeth. Urosomites 1-3 bicarinate. Telson each lobe with 2 long and 1-2 short apical robust setae, inner margins smooth. (RBZ 64: 351–359)
Reference:
Hughes LE, Kaji T (2016) RBZ 64: 351–359. 
https://zenodo.org/records/5355546

Description: Female, 2.37 mm. Head and body normal for genus, eyes round. Antenna 1: Length ratio of peduncle articles 1,2,3-20:23:14; flagellum with 6 articles. Antenna 2: Articles 4 and 5 subequal in length; flagellum with 5 articles; antenna 2, 0.8 times the length of antenna 1. Gnathopod 1: Coxa suboval; article 2 elongate with 3 anteromarginal spines; article 4 with 2 posterodistal spines; article 5 with spinose posterior lobe reaching along half of hind margin on article 6; palm transverse, corner defined by 2 stout spines; inner margin of dactyl serrulate proximally. Gnathopod 2: Coxa subquadrate; posterior margin of article 4 with 2-3 stout spines, distal edge with 1 long spine; article 5 with elongate posterior lobe reaching 90% as long as hind margin on article 6; article 6 distally expanded, anterior edge of outer face with 1-2 submarginal spines, otherwise unarmed; palm transverse with a row of minute spines, corner defined by 2 stout spines; dactyl attenuate, inner margin serrate on upper half. Epimera: Corners of plates unproduced, ventral margins of plates 2 and 3 with 2 spines each. Uropod 1: Peduncle longer than either 2 or 3, outer margin with 5 spines, inner with 1 distal spine; rami lanceolate, outer slightly shorter, with 3 outer and 1 inner marginal spines on distal part of ramus; inner ramus with 4 inner and 3 outer marginal spines.(McKinney 1978: 140–143)
Reference: McKinney LD (1978) Gulf Research Reports 6(2): 137–143. https://aquila.usm.edu/gcr/vol6/iss2/4/

Diagnosis: Antennae 1 and 2 subequal in length, antenna 1 with extended basal articles, flagellum articles with aesthetascs; accessory flagellum 1-segmented, similar in size to basal article 3; antenna 2 with articles 3 and 4 long; mandibular molar large, with ridged and toothed triturating surfaces, numerous setae of same size around external margin; gnathopod 1 subchelate, with carpus lobate and not reaching propodus distal margin, palm with regular and homogenous distribution of same-sized setae; gnathopod 2 subchelate without robust setae on margin, with carpus lobate, reaching distal margin of propodus, palms of both gnathopods 1 and 2 with regular and homogenous distribution of same-sized setae and 2 stout robust setae delimiting the palm. Telson triangular, entire, longer than wide, wider in proximal region, with rounded apex. (Nauplius 21(2): 195–204)
Reference: Leite FPP, Siqueira SGL (2013) Nauplius 21(2): 195–204. https://doi.org/10.1590/S0104-64972013000200006
Reid DM (1951) Bull. Amer. Mus. Nat. Hist. 95(2): 101–206.

Diagnosis: Pereopods 3–7, dactyls with distinct inner marginal tooth at unguis; antenna 1, peduncular article 2 slightly longer than peduncular article 1; gnathopod 2, posterodistal corner of basis with seta, lacking spine; epimeron 1–2, posteroventral corners pointed; mandibular palp, article 3 1.67 x length of article 2; maxilliped palp, lateral margin of palp article 1 setose with 8 strong setae; telson, linguiform, 2.1 x as long as wide, apically narrowly rounded not acute. (Kim et al. 2010, Zootaxa 2477: 21–36)
Remarks: Hourstonius geojeensis however, is distinguished from its congeners by the inner marginal tooth of the pereopod dactyls as well as characters listed in table 2 and the key (page 11). Hourstonius japonica and H. vilordes differ by having a posterodistal spine and not a seta on the basis of gnathopod 2. As well, H. breviculus has smooth posteroventral corners on epimeron 1–2, while the new species has pointed corners.
Reference: Kim YH, Hendrycks JA, Lee KS (2010) Zootaxa 2477: 21–36.

Remarks: H. japonica and H. vilordes differ [from H. geojeensis] by having a posterodistal spine and not a seta on the basis of gnathopod 2." + Hirayama (1983): "The present species [H. japonica] is closely related to Gitanopsis vilordes but is clearly distinguished from it by the following points; (1) accessory flagellum uniarticulate, (2) anterior head lobe acute, (3) posterior extension of carpus of gnathopod 1 reaching three fourths of posterior margin of propod." + Barnard (1970): "G. vilordes ... differ[s] from G. pele and G. tortugae in [its] large gnathopods with article 6 wider than [its] coxae and strongly expanded distally. Kim et al. (2010)
Reference: Barnard JL (1962) Pacific Naturalist 3(14) (original); Hirayama (1983) PSMBL 28(5/6); Kim et al. (2010) Zootaxa 2477.

Diagnosis: Gitanopsis pusilla K. H. Barnard (1916) from South Africa and G. vilordes J. L. Barnard (1962c) from California differ from G. pele and G. tortugae in their large gnathopods with article 6 wider than their coxae and strongly expanded distally.
Reference: Barnard KH (1916) Ann. S. Afr. Mus. 15 (original); Barnard (1970) Smithson. Contr. Zool. 34.

Remarks: The present species is closely similar to Gitanopsis baciroa J.L. Barnard, 1979 from the Gulf of California and Galapagos Islands and the Japanese gitanopsids (Hirayama, 1983), G. brevicula Hirayama, 1983, G. japonica Hirayama, 1983, G. robastodentes Hirayama, 1983 and G. longa Hirayama, 1983, in the following characteristics: 1) the rostrum reaches the distal end of the peduncular article 1 of antenna 1; 2) the inner plate of maxilla 2 has ca. 10 distal setae; 3) the molar process of the mandible is medium ...; 4) the carpus lobe of gnathopod 2 nearly or just reaches the palmar defining spines. Of the above five species, the shape of the telson, of which the length is equal to or a little shorter than twice the basal width, indicates that the present species is more closely related to Gitanopsis baciroa and G. brevicuta than to the other three species. ... the basis [of gnathopod 2 in the present species] is prominently extended posterodistally. Thus, the present species is clearly distinguished from these two species in the feature of gnathopod 2.(Hirayama & Takeuchi 1993)
Reference: Hirayama A, Takeuchi I (1993) PSMBL 36(3): 141–178. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176228
Alves J, Neves EG, Johnsson R (2024) JMBA UK 104: e26. https://doi.org/10.1017/S002531542400016X

Remarks: The present species is closely related to Gitanopsis vilordes (J.L. Barnard 1962d) and G. japonica sp. nov., but differs from both in that the carpus of gnathopod 2 extends posteriorly beyond the posterior margin of the propod (Hirayama, 1983).
Reference: Hirayama A (1983) PSMBL 28(5/6): 75–150. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176060

Remarks: The present species resembles Gitanopsis pele (J.L. Barnard 1970b) in the gnathopods, maxilla 2, telson, and other features. It differs, however, in having one small posteroventral tooth on pleonal epimerons 1–2, only two stout teeth on the shoulders of the lower lip, and a subsymmetrical upper lip (Hirayama, 1983).
Reference: Hirayama A (1983) PSMBL 28(5/6): 75–150. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176060

Remarks: The new species resembles Gitanopsis vilordes (J.L. Barnard 1962d) and other Japanese Gitanopsis spp. that have an elongate telson, but differs distinctly in having one stout tooth, rather than a spine, at the posterodistal end of the basis of gnathopod 1 (Hirayama, 1983).
Reference: Hirayama A (1983) PSMBL 28(5/6): 75–150. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176060

Diagnosis: The body lacks dorsal cusps, and the lateral cephalic lobe is broadly rounded. The eye is large, with a black-pigment core in alcohol, and the antennae extend subequally. Gnathopods are small, but their palms are strong and nearly transverse. On gnathopod 1, the stout lobe of article 5 reaches about halfway along article 6; on gnathopod 2, it extends about 75–85 percent along article 6. The sixth articles are weakly expanded distally, much longer than broad, and about half as broad as their coxae; the dactyls are proximally pectinate along their inner edges. Coxa 1 tapers distally and is subconical, with a serrate posteroventral corner; coxa 2 has 1 small posteroventral notch. The mandibular molar is large, cushion-shaped, and strongly triturative. The outer plate of the maxilliped has a slightly excavate and pectinate mediodistal margin, as in Gitanogeiton and Gitanopsis tortugae. The dactyls of pereopods 1–5 are simple. Pleonal epimera 1–2 each bear a small posteroventral tooth, while epimeron 3 is rounded-quadrate posteroventrally. The telson is of medium length, about 60 percent as long as the peduncle of uropod 3, and rounded apically but coniform (Barnard 1970).
Reference: Barnard JL (1970) Smithson. Contr. Zool. 34: 1–286. https://repository.si.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/b61987f2-f27d-4fed-ae5b-eada1f5ec461/content

Remarks: Although the present species resembles Gitanopsis vilordes (J.L. Barnard 1962d) in its gnathopods, telson, and other features, it is clearly distinguished by the following characters: (1) the accessory flagellum is uniarticulate; (2) the anterior head lobe is acute; and (3) the posterior extension of the carpus of gnathopod 1 reaches three fourths of the posterior margin of the propod. The present species also differs from G. vilordes (Nagata 1965a) in that the posterodistal end of the basis of gnathopod 2 lacks spines (Hirayama, 1983).
Reference: Hirayama A (1983) PSMBL 28(5/6): 75–150. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176060
Ortiz M, Lalana R (1995) Avicennia (Cuba).

Diagnosis: Gitanopsis pele is distinguished from G. tortugae mainly by two minor characters: (1) the serrations on coxae 1–2 and (2) the large eyes (Barnard, 1970). Valencia et al. (2023) also state that H. baciroa differs from H. tortugae because the propodus of the latter’s G2 lacks submarginal robust setae on the anterolateral surface.
Reference: Shoemaker CR (1933) J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 23: 248 (original); Barnard (1970) Smithson. Contr. Zool. 34.
Karaman G (1980) Poljopr. šumar. 26: 23–64.

Description: The anterior head lobe is rounded, and the antennae are short and subequal. Coxa 1 is reduced, distinctly shorter than and mostly concealed by the following coxa. Coxa 2 is rounded ventrally and bears small ornamentations. G1 and G2 are stout and strongly subchelate, with a strongly inflated propodus and a slender dactylus finely pectinate behind. The carpal lobe of G1 is spinose, and the palm margin bears robust setae. The carpal lobe of G2 bears three to four distal robust setae, is elongated, and extends fully to the posterior angle of the propodus; the propodus has two robust setae on its anterolateral surface and paired robust setae defining the palm. The rami of U1 are markedly unequal. U2 is shorter than U1 and U3. U3 is biramous, with both rami 1-articulate. T is longer than wide but much shorter than the peduncle of U3 (Valencia et al. 2023).
Remarks: Hourstonius baciroa resembles H. vilordes (Barnard, 1962), reported from southern California, as well as H. laguna (McKinney, 1978) and H. tortugae (Shoemaker, 1942), reported from the Caribbean coast of Colombia. Four robust setae on the carpal lobe of G2 are present in Hourstonius baciroa but absent in H. vilordes. In H. baciroa, the carpal lobe of G2 reaches fully to the posterior margin of the propodus, whereas in H. laguna it is short, extending along three-fourths of the posterior margin of the propodus. Coxa 2 is rounded in H. baciroa, but quadrate in H. laguna and H. vilordes (Valencia et al. 2023).
Reference: Valencia B, Cobo-Viveros AM, Lazarus JF, Giraldo A (2023) SciELO Preprints 5955. https://doi.org/10.1590/SciELOPreprints.5955

Diagnosis: From Pacific Mexico, Gitanopsis pusilloides Shoemaker (1942) is distinguished from G. pele and G. tortugae by the very short processes on article 5 of the gnathopods and the more strongly transverse palms (Barnard, 1970).
Reference: Shoemaker CR (1942) (original); Barnard (1970) Smithson. Contr. Zool. 34.

Diagnosis: Apolochus cresti appears most closely related to Apolochus neapolitanus (Della Valle, 1893), as illustrated by Krapp-Schickel (1982) from the Mediterranean. It is distinguished from A. neapolitanus by (1) the shape of the lateral cephalic lobe (rounded vs. truncated, respectively), (2) the shape of the molar process, (3) the proportion of mandible palp article 3 (longer than the previous two articles combined in A. cresti vs. shorter in A. neapolitanus), and (4) the carpal lobe of gnathopod 2 (just reaching the corner of the palm in A. cresti vs. slightly passing the corner of the palm in A. neapolitanus) (Morales-Núñez & Chigbu, 2016).
Reference: Morales-Núñez AG, Chigbu P (2016) ZooKeys 571: 81–104. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.571.7440

Description: Female, 3.15 mm. Head and body are typical of the genus. Eyes are circular, with a black center surrounded by numerous opaque ommatidia. Antenna 1: Peduncular article 2 is 1.3 times as long as article 1 and 3 times as long as article 3. The flagellum has 8 articles, each with 1-2 elongate, flattened setae at its distoventral corner; the uniarticulate accessory flagellum is subequal in length to the first flagellar article. Antenna 2: Peduncular article 5 is 1.3 times as long as article 4. Articles 4 and 5 bear distal spines, and article 5 has a medial row of 4 short spines. The flagellum has 11 articles. ... Gnathopod 1: The coxa is suboval and partly concealed by the following coxa; article 2 is elongate. Article 4 bears 1 medial spine on the posterior margin and 6 distal spines. Article 5 has a spinose posterior lobe. Article 6 bears 1 anterodistal and 2 mediofacial spines, and its serrate, transverse palm is lined with 6 slender spines and defined by 2 stout spines. The inner margin of the dactyl is serrate. Gnathopod 2: Article 4 bears a stout mediomarginal spine and 2 distal spines. Article 5 has an elongate posterior lobe that reaches the edge of the palm; the lobe's outer margin bears 3 basal spines, and its distal part is spinose. Article 6 is distally expanded, with 1-2 submarginal spines on the outer face. The palm is transverse and serrate, lined with slender spines, and has a corner defined by 2 stout spines. The inner margin of the dactyl is serrate, and the dactyl is distally attenuate (McKinney 1978: 137–138).
Reference: McKinney LD (1978) Gulf Research Reports 6(2): 137–143. https://aquila.usm.edu/gcr/vol6/iss2/4/

Diagnosis: Female 2.55. In all respects, resembles A. casahoya except as follows: article 6 of gnathopod 2 has 4 submarginal spines along its outer margin; the peduncle of uropod 1 bears 5 slender spines on the inner margin and 10 stout spines on the outer margin; the inner ramus of uropod 1 has 5 spines on each margin; the subequal outer ramus has a basally setulose inner margin with 3 distal spines and an outer margin bearing 8 stout, curved spines; the inner ramus of uropod 2 is armed with 4 spines on the inner margin and 5 on the outer margin, while the outer ramus has 4 spines on the outer margin (McKinney 1978).
Reference: McKinney LD (1978) Gulf Research Reports 6(2): 137–143. https://aquila.usm.edu/gcr/vol6/iss2/4/

Remarks: The new species does not correspond to any species in the “pleonal tooth formulas of species in genus Melita” presented by J.L. Barnard (1962a, p. 107). It is readily distinguished from all other species by its dorsal appearance, gnathopods 1–2, pleonal epimera, and telson (Nagata, 1965).
Reference: Nagata K (1965) PSMBL 13(4): 291–326. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/175410

Remarks: The new species shares several characteristics with Melita valesi, M. koreana, M. laevidorsum, M. pahuwai, M. oregonensis, M. nitida, M. zeylanica, and M. zeylanica kauerti: the pleon and urosomite 1 lack dorsoposterior armature, and the outer ramus of uropod 1 lacks a terminal segment. It is, however, clearly distinguishable from the latter taxa by the structure of the dactyls of pereopods 1–2, which are elongate and feeble in the present species (Hirayama, 1987).
Reference: Hirayama A (1987) PSMBL 32(1/3): 1–62. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176135

Remarks: This new species is similar to M. koreana and M. nagatai, but differs from both in the shapes of male gnathopod 1 and female coxa 6. It also has the following minor characteristics: epimeral plate 3 is rather distinctly produced ventrodistally; the dorsal side of urosomite 2 is rather distinctly toothed; the telson bears lateral spines in large specimens; the antennae are weakly spinose; and the dorsal side of the mandible palp has weak setation (Yamato, 1987).
Reference: Yamato S (1987) PSMBL 32(4/6): 275–302. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176142

Diagnosis: Melita nagatai resembles M. bingoensis Yamato, 1987, but is readily distinguished by the absence of medial robust setae on the propodus of gnathopod 1. It also closely resembles M. koreana Stephensen, 1944 ... M. nagatai differs morphologically from M. koreana in having (1) an acute triangular lobe anterodistally on the propodus of gnathopod 1 and (2) epimeral plates 1–3 that are slightly acute ventrodistally (Kim et al., 2023).
Remarks: This new species closely resembles Melita koreana, but differs from it in the distally acute anterodistal lobe and trapezoidal excavation of article 6 of male gnathopod 1, and in the broader and stronger projection of female coxa 6. It also differs from M. koreana in minor features: a slender body form, slightly smaller body size, a slightly toothed urosomite 2, and a slightly acute epimeral plate 3. Kim et al. (2023, supplementary) also note that Melita nagatai resembles M. bingoensis Yamato, 1987, but is readily distinguished by lacking medial robust setae on the propodus of gnathopod 1. They state that M. nagatai also closely resembles M. koreana Stephensen, 1944 ... and differs morphologically from M. koreana in having an acute triangular lobe anterodistally on the propodus of gnathopod 1 and epimeral plates 1–3 that are slightly acute ventrodistally (Yamato, 1987; Kim et al., 2023).
Reference: Yamato S (1987) PSMBL 32(4/6): 275–302. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176142 | Kim K-W et al. (2023) J. Species Res. 12(1): 1–26.

Remarks: My specimens are consistent with Stephensen’s original description. ... However, my specimens ... also agreed well with Stephensen’s description regarding the absence of dorsal teeth and teeth on epimeral plate 3. These features can therefore serve as diagnostic characters for M. koreana. ... M. koreana lacks stout spines on article 6 of male gnathopod 1 (unlike M. bingoensis) and has a uni-articulate uropod 3 bearing only three apical spines (unlike M. rylovae) (Yamato, 1987).
Reference: Yamato S (1987) PSMBL 32(4/6): 275–302. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176142  | Original: Stephensen K 1944, Vidensk. Meddr dansk naturh. Foren. 108: 191–212.

Diagnosis: In males, the gnathopod 2 propodus has an oblique palmar margin, and the outer ramus of uropod 3 is uni-articulate and weakly arched, measures 7–8 times its width, and lacks long setae. In females, the anterior lobe of the pereopod 6 coxa is deep and strongly hooked (Tomikawa et al., 2018).
Reference: Tomikawa K, Hirashima K, Hirai A, Uchiyama R (2018) ZooKeys 760: 73–88. https://doi.org/10.3897/zookeys.760.24778 | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5986893/

Diagnosis: The head bears a minute rostrum, and its lateral cephalic lobes are rounded, with noth; the eyes are medium-sized and suboval. Pleon segments 1–3 have smooth dorsal surfaces, without medial dorsal teeth. Urosomite 1 is smooth dorsally, whereas urosomite 2 bears two short, stout setae on each side of the middorsal line. The telson lobes have subapical notches. Antenna 1 has a very short, 1+ articulated accessory flagellum. The facial setal row is absent from the inner plate of maxilla 2. In the male, the propodus of pereopod 1 is excavated at the basal part of the palmar margin and has a distinct protuberance at mid-length; the distal palmar margin is short and roundly convex. The dactylus of male pereopod 1 is short and bears a tri-lobed process on its inner margin. The propodus of male pereopod 2 is oval and elongated, without a clear palmar corner; its palm is oblique, serrate, and slightly tuberculate. In the female, the anterior lobe of coxa 6 is very long and hooked, with a distorted apical part. The outer ramus of uropod 3 is 1-segmented and elongated, with 3–4 groups of stout setae along both lateral and median margins (Labay 2016).
Remarks: All examined specimens agree with Ueno’s (1940a) original description of this species, particularly in the shape of the lateral head lobes, the 2-articulate accessory flagellum of antenna 1, the presence of a dactylar process on male gnathopod 1, and the elongate article 6 and setulose article 3 of male gnathopod 2. Because these characteristics are peculiar to this species among the known members of the genus Melita, I have identified the present material as this species (Yamato 1988).
Reference: Labay VS (2016) Zootaxa 4156(1): 1–73. https://treatment.plazi.org/id/995B87D6FFD6FF8DFF3AF88AC72A02E4 | Yamato S (1988) PSMBL 33(1/3): 79–95. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176148

Remarks: The setosity of pereopods 6–7 and uropod 3 distinguishes this new species (Yamato, 1990).
Reference: Yamato S (1990) PSMBL 34(4/6): 149–165. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176168

Remarks: The new species closely resembles Melita inaequistylis (Dana, 1852) in lacking dorsal teeth on the pleon and urosomite 1, having pleonal epimeron 3 extended backward ventrally, and possessing a biarticulate outer ramus on uropod 3. However, it differs from M. inaequistylis, in which the dorsodistal end of urosomite 2 bears 2 sets of 2 teeth and 1 spine, and the anterior head lobe has 1 small ventral notch. The new species also differs distinctly from the latter species [M. awa, M. latimerus, M. matilda, M. nitida]: in those species, the propodus of gnathopod 1 lacks an anterodistal process, its palm is oblique or almost transverse against it and defined by a rounded process, pleonal epimeron 3 is subrectangular, and the mandibular palp is feeble or medium (Hirayama, 1987).
Reference: Hirayama A (1987) PSMBL 32(1/3): 1–62. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176135

Remarks: Within the genus Melita, this new species is unique in having a cluster of two basofacial spines on the peduncle of uropod 1 ... It is also characterized by a strongly spinated telson, a biarticulate outer ramus of uropod 3, and a dorsolateral tooth on each side of urosomite 2. ... However, the three species [M. hoshinoi, M. rylovae, M. pilopropoda] are readily distinguished by the shape of article 6 of male gnathopod 1. In M. rylovae, article 6 bears several robust palmar spines and a quadrate anterodistal lobe; in M. pilopropoda, it bears two stout spines near the hollow of the inner surface and a small falcate anterodistal lobe; and in this new species, it bears one small spine at the palmar corner and a roundly produced anterodistal lobe (Yamato, 1990).
Reference: Yamato S (1990) PSMBL 34(4/6): 149–165. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176168

Remarks: The biarticulation of the uropod 3 is a distinctive characteristic of M. rylovae that remains unchanged during development. As noted in the Discussion, M. rylovae has a biarticulate, broad outer ramus of uropod 3; spination of the telson; arch-shaped dorsal teeth on pleosomites 1–3; and no lateral setae on the palp of maxilla 1. My specimens also agree with Bulycheva’s original description in the following distinctive characteristics: a broad outer ramus of uropod 3, a strongly spinated telson, arch-shaped dorsal teeth on the pleosomites, a robust article 4 of pereopods 5–7, the shapes of the gnathopods, and the shape of the hooked coxa 6 in the female (Yamato, 1987).
Reference: Yamato S (1987) PSMBL 32(4/6): 275–302. https://repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dspace/handle/2433/176142 | Original: Bulyčeva 1955

Remarks: V. tinggiensis is one of the eyed species; its specific distinguishing characters are given in the key context of the satsumaensis paper (Lim et al., 2010).
Reference: Lim JHC, Azman BAR, Othman BHR (2010) Zootaxa 2348: 23–39.

Diagnosis: Victoriopisa ryukyuensis, known from Okinawa Island, southern Japan, resembles V. satsumaensis sp. nov. However, V. satsumaensis sp. nov. differs clearly from V. ryukyuensis in the following characters (those of V. ryukyuensis in parentheses): (1) antenna 1 lacks a distodorsal tuft of long setae on peduncular article 2 (tuft present); (2) the palmar margin of gnathopod 2 bears 2 projections (1 projection); (3) the posterior margin of the gnathopod 2 dactylus has a proximal projection and a median excavation (a proximal excavation followed by a projection); and (4) epimeral plates 1 and 3, and often plate 2, have minute acute teeth at the posteroventral corners (no teeth) (Tomikawa & Yamada, 2026).
Reference: Tomikawa K, Yamada R (2026) Species Diversity 31(1). https://www.vliz.be/imisdocs/publications/ocrd/422451.pdf | Original: Morino H 1991

Remarks: In male V. australiensis, gnathopod 2 has a short carpus, and the propodal palm is broadly excavate and lacks a border of robust setae. By contrast, in V. marina the carpus is compressed, and the palm is narrowly excavate and bordered by robust setae. Pereopod 7 of Victoriopisa australiensis has a large, broadly expanded basis and merus, with numerous slender setae distally; in V. marina, the basis and merus are narrower, and the distal part of the pereopod is not nearly as setose (Lowry & Springthorpe, 2005).
Reference: Lowry JK, Springthorpe RT (2005) Rec. Aust. Mus. 57(2): 237–302. https://journals.australian.museum/media/Uploads/Journals/18020/1463_complete.pdf

Diagnosis: The mandible, depicted by Griffiths (1974a, fig. 4b) as lacking elements between the pars incisiva and pars molaris, actually bears a row of spines exactly comparable to that of the new species ... The inner lobe of the posterior maxilla bears an oblique row of setae ... these two characters ... now allow the species V. epistomata to be definitively incorporated into the Eriopisa lineage (Stock & Platvoet, 1981: 29).
Reference: Stock JH, Platvoet D (1981) Bull. Zool. Mus. 8(3): 21–30. https://repository.naturalis.nl/pub/505431 | Original: Griffiths CL 1974, Ann. S. Afr. Mus. 66: 131–138.

Remarks: The most conspicuous differences between Victoriopisa australiensis and V. marina are in the male gnathopod 2 and pereopod 7. In V. australiensis, gnathopod 2 has a short carpus, and the propodus palm is broadly excavate and lacks a border of robust setae; in V. marina, the carpus is compressed, and the palm is narrowly excavate and bordered by robust setae. Pereopod 7 of V. australiensis has a large, broadly expanded basis and merus, bearing many slender setae distally. In V. marina, the basis and merus are narrower, and the distal part of the pereopod is not nearly as setose. Victoriopisa marina most closely resembles species of Victoriopisa with slender seventh pereopods, but differs from all of them in the extremely broadened palm of gnathopod 1 and the shape of the palm of gnathopod 2 (Lowry & Springthorpe 2005).
Reference: Lowry JK, Springthorpe RT (2005) Rec. Aust. Mus. 57(2): 237–302. https://journals.australian.museum/media/Uploads/Journals/18020/1463_complete.pdf

Diagnosis: V. satsumaensis is further distinguished from V. papiae by the following characters (those of the latter species are given in parentheses): (1) the inner plate of maxilla 1 bears 16–19 setae along the distal margin (7 setae); (2) the palmar margin of gnathopod 2 has 2 large proximal robust setae and 2 subdistal projections (3 projections, the proximal 2 each with large robust setae); and (3) the dactylus of gnathopod 2 has a median excavation on the posterior margin (a median projection) (Tomikawa & Yamada, 2026).
Reference: Tomikawa K, Yamada R (2026) Species Diversity 31(1). | Original: Asari KP 1983, Bull. Mus. natn. Hist. nat., Paris, 4e sér., 5, sect. A(3): 851–869.

Diagnosis: It differs from V. chilkensis (Chilton, 1921) and V. australiensis (Chilton, 1923) in the carpal article of the first gnathopod: this article is elongate in both Indo-Pacific species but triangular in the new Atlantic species. The basal article of P7 bears several long setae in V. atlantica. The telson of V. australiensis is neither described nor illustrated; that of V. chilkensis differs from that of V. atlantica by the absence of lateral spines. In all the characters listed above, the new species closely resembles V. epistomata (Griffiths, 1974) (Stock & Platvoet, 1981: 28).
Reference: Stock JH, Platvoet D (1981) Bull. Zool. Mus. 8(3): 21–30. https://repository.naturalis.nl/pub/505431

Remarks: Hirayama (1992).
Hirayama A (1992), Asian Marine Biology 9: 139–166 (Hirayama, 1992).
Hirayama A (1992) Asian Marine Biology 9: 139–166. (Hirayama, 1992)
Hirayama A (1992) Asian Marine Biology 9: 139–166 (Hirayama, 1992).

Description: The head’s anterolateral angles are moderately acute, and the rostrum is not prominent. The eyes are very large. The dorsal hinge margins of the paraeon and pleon segments are entire. Side plates 1–4 have a few indents along their lower margins. The posteroinferior angles of pleon segments 2 and 3 project briefly as acute points. In antenna 1, the first joint is stout, the second is much more slender and ⅓ the length of the first, and the third is ½ the length of the second. The male flagellum has 17 joints. In the male, gnathopod 1 has a long second joint and a fifth joint that broadens towards the base. The sixth joint is as long as the fifth and bears free spines along its inner margin; the seventh joint is curved. Gnathopod 2 is considerably stronger, with a triangular fifth joint whose lower end is fringed with small spines, and a rather large sixth joint. In uropods 1 and 2, the peduncle has 1 apical spinule... The telson is short and entire (Thacker et al., 2023).
Reference: Bussarawich S (1985) PMBC Mangrove Ecology Seminar 5: 1–15 (Thai record); Thacker et al. (2023) Zootaxa 5340(1)

Description: The body is slender. Paired posterodorsal teeth are present on pleon segments 1–3 and urosome segments 1–2. The head is longer than the first paraeon segment, and the ocular lobes are rounded. The eyes are dark and lie near the margin of the head... In the male, the second joint of antenna 1 is slightly longer than the first; in the female, the two joints are sub-equal. The third joint is small. The flagellum is about 3 times as long as the peduncle and has 32 joints, while the accessory flagellum has about 8 joints... Gnathopod 2 is long. The fifth joint is considerably larger than the sixth and is strongly fringed along and near the hind margin, with groups of spines set on the inner surface. The sixth joint is oblong-oval; the palm is very short and transversely rounded, and is not overlapped by the small finger. (Bussarawich, 1985; Thacker et al., 2024)
Reference: Bussarawich (1985); Thacker et al. (2024) Zootaxa 5446(3): 398–402

Description: The body is compressed. The paraeon and pleon segments are dorsally non-dentate, except that pleon segment 5 bears a submedian fascicle of 2–3 spines on each side. In the female, side plate 6 has a distinct hook. The posteroinferior angle of pleon segment 3 has a short protrusion... In the male, gnathopod 2 is very large: the 5th joint is cup-like, with a group of setae along the hind margin, and the 6th joint is massive and oblong, with a smooth outer surface but a densely setiferous inner surface and hind margin. The strong finger is half the length of the 6th joint... The telson comprises two quite separate plates terminating in a sharp apex, with five spines apically and 2–3 spines along the sides (Bussarawich, 1985; Lowry & Myers, 2019).
Reference: Bussarawich (1985); Lowry & Myers (2019) redescription

Description: The rostral tip is small and rounded-conical. The apex of the first side plate of the paraeon segment bears a fringe of three plumose setae. The pleon is fully segmented, and the lateral margins of the first two segments are fringed with plumose setae. The eyes are small and dark... In gnathopod 2, the fourth joint bears the usual double row of extremely long setae... The sixth joint is narrowly oblong and slightly curved, with an oblique series of long setae fringing it near the base. The short, robust finger is tridentate, with upturned teeth; the third tooth is the largest and forms the unguis. Uropod 1 has two coupling teeth at the inner angle of the broad peduncle... The telson is broader than long, apically rounded, and tubular, widening at each corner of the base (Bussarawich, 1985).
Reference: Bussarawich (1985) — first record for Thailand

Description: Antenna 1 is slender and measures ¾ the length of antenna 2; its flagellum has 14 joints. The flagellum of antenna 2 is longer than the peduncle and has 20 joints. In the male, the 2nd joint of gnathopod 1 is not much expanded; the 4th, 5th, and 6th joints bear setae along the lower distal end, and the 6th joint has two spines where the tip of the finger meets the palm; the 7th joint fits the palm... In the male, the 2nd joint of gnathopod 2 is not much expanded, and its lower front margin has a small, rounded lobe... The 6th joint is large and oval, with an oblique, setose palm... Uropod 3 is little longer than the outer ramus and reaches the end of the telson; the inner ramus is small and scale-like... The telson is cleft to the base, with the lobes widely gaping (Lowry & Myers, 2019).
Reference: Bussarawich (1985); Lowry & Myers (2019) redescription

Diagnosis: Antenna 1 has 3 short flagellar articles and reaches ¼ of peduncular article 5 of antenna 2; antenna 2 has more than 12 flagellar articles. The anterior coxal lobe of pereopod 6 is not well developed. In the female, the right lacinia mobilis of the mandible is 6-dentate. The distomedial lobe of maxilliped palp article 2 is well developed, while article 4 is reduced and button-shaped. Gnathopod 1 is parachelate; in the male, the posterior margins of the carpus and propodus each bear a lobe covered with palmate setae... Gnathopod 2 is subchelate in the male and mitten-shaped in the female... Epimera 2–3 bear a stridulating organ just above the ventral margins (Azman et al., 2014).
Reference: Azman et al. (2014) ZSE 90(1): 7–19
Chilton (1925) Tale Sap; Thacker et al. (2023) Zootaxa 5340(1)

Description: The head is free and not coalesced with peraeonite 1; the eye is present and large. The body is laterally compressed... Coxae 1–4 are longer than broad and overlapping. Gnathopod 1 is subequal to gnathopod 2, and gnathopod 2 is subchelate. Pereopod 5 is shorter than pereopod 6. Article 2 of pereopod 5 is expanded into a subrectangular... Uropod 2 bears a ventromedial spur, and its inner ramus is subequal to the outer ramus. The telson is laminar, cleft, and longer than broad (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2009) Nat. Hist. J. Chulalongkorn Univ. 9(1): 69–83
Chilton (1925) Tale Sap; Lowry & Myers (2017) neotype

Description: In the male, the carpus of gnathopod 1 is large; its posterodistal corner extends into a large conical tooth, and its inner surface bears a small accessory tooth. The dactylus has a smooth inner margin with a few small hairs and is expanded proximally (Chilton, 1925; Thacker et al., 2025).
Reference: Chilton (1925) Tale Sap; Thacker et al. (2025) Zootaxa

Diagnosis: In males, a ventral process is present on the pereon. On gnathopod 1, the ischium and merus lack posterodistal projections; the carpus bears 3 teeth, of which the middle tooth is large, and the propodus broadens distally. On gnathopod 2, the coxa has a posteromedial projection, the basis is straight, and the carpus is longer than the propodus; the propodus bears several robust setae at the posterodistal corner and along the posterior margin. The peduncle of uropod 1 bears an inter-ramal process (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Description:
Head. The head is approximately as long as the first 2 pereonites. The rostrum is undeveloped, the inferior antennal sinus is moderately deep and concave, measuring 0.3 times the head length, and the eye is distinct. Antenna 1 is slightly longer than antenna 2; peduncular articles 1–3 have a length ratio of 1: 1.7: 1.1. Article 1 is slender and bears 2 posteromarginal spines. The flagellum has 22 articles and is 1.4 times the peduncle length; the short accessory flagellum is uni-articulate. Antenna 2 has a stout peduncle with 4 segments in the ratio 1: 3: 10: 7. The inner margin of article 3 bears 3 robust setae, and 2 robust setae are present posterodistally. Article 5 is shorter than article 4. The short flagellum is subequal in length to peduncular article 5 and comprises 7 articles; each of articles 2–7 bears a pair of curved, bifid robust setae. The upper lip or labrum is rounded and broad, with a small median depression and pubescence on each lobe. The inner plates of the lower lip are well developed and subtriangular; the mandibular process is narrow but well developed. The outer plate bears arborescent setae on the inner face of the outer lobe and is covered with thin hairs. The mandibles are alike except for the number of accessory blades: 4 on the right and 5 on the left. The right incisor has 4 dentates and the left incisor 5 dentates; the lacinia mobilis bears 4 teeth on the left and 5 on the right. The molar process is medium-sized, distally ridged and marginally serrate, and bears a single seta. The palp is triarticulate, with article lengths in the ratio 1: 1.2: 1.1; article 3 bears apical and marginal setae. Maxilla 1 has a small inner plate; the outer plate bears 8 apical robust setae. The palp extends beyond the outer plate, is biarticulate, and bears 6 apical spines. On maxilla 2, the inner plate has a mediofacial row of 25 slender setae and one robust seta at the middle, while its outer margin is naked; the outer plate is subequal in size to the inner plate. The maxilliped has a broad, short inner plate, apically furnished with several plumose setae and 3 marginal setae. Its broad outer plate nearly reaches palp article 2 and bears 13 marginal spines. The palp is 4-articulate, with article lengths in the ratio 2: 3: 3.2: 1.

Pereon. Gnathopod 1 is carpochelate and larger than gnathopod 2. Its coxal plate is subrectangular, with a ventral process on the inner side. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 7.8: 1: 2.7: 8: 3.5: 3.5. The basis is slender, 3.9 times as long as broad, with a straight anterior margin and one fine seta on the posteriodistal margin. The ischium is short and subrectangular; the merus is trapezoidal and produced anterodistally. The carpus is 1.6 times as long as broad, with a produced posterodistal corner bearing a tooth and a smaller tooth on the inner face; its setose posterior margin has a small tooth. The propodus is subequal in length to the dactylus and 0.5 times the carpus length; its posterior margin is proximally concave and distally expanded. The dactylus is fairly curved, with a concave distal end and 2 robust setae. Gnathopod 2 is subchelate. The coxal plate is shallow, with its ventral margins produced posteriorly into a triangular expansion. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 4.6: 1: 1.7: 3.8: 3.3: 1.8. The slender basis is as long as articles 5 and 6 combined; its anterior margin is straight and bears 6 fine setae. The ischium is subrectangular, and the merus trapezoidal, with a produced posterodistal angle and long setae on the posterior margin. The carpus is 2.5 times as long as wide; its crenulate posterior margin bears 25 dense setae. The propodal palmar margin is transverse and finely setose, with a bifid robust seta at the posterodistal corner and 2 bifid robust setae on the posterior margin. The dactylus is slightly longer than the palmar margin and has a crenulate inner margin with several fine setules.

Pereopod 3 is slender, with a small, subquadrate coxal plate. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 4.8: 1: 2.5: 1.7: 1.7: 1.2. The slender basis is sparsely setose along the anterior and posterior margins and at the posterodistal corner. The ischium is short and subrectangular; the merus is slightly produced anterodistally. The carpus is suboval, with a setose posterior margin. The narrow propodus bears setae on both margins, and the long, thin dactylus is shorter than the propodus. Pereopod 4 resembles pereopod 3; its coxal plate has a triangular medial projection of the ventral margin. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 4.1: 1: 2.5: 1.4: 1.6: 1.1. The slender basis bears short setae on the anterior margin. The ischium is short and subrectangular, and the merus is slightly produced anterodistally. The oval carpus bears setae on both margins; the long, narrow propodus is setose on both anterior and posterior margins. The dactylus is long and thin. On pereopod 5, the coxa is expanded posteroventrally into a long, narrowly obtuse angle. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 5.8: 1: 2.2: 1.8: 0.8. The basis is subrectangular, with fine setae along the anterior margin; the ischium is short. The carpus bears two robust setae along the posterior margin and on the posterodistally. The propodus bears four robust setae along the posterior margin, and the dactylus is short and strongly curved. Pereopod 6 is elongate, 1.6 times as long as pereopod 5, and has a coxa produced posteriorly into a rounded lobe. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 3.7: 1: 2.7: 1.7: 3.3: 1. The basis is almost linear and bears 7 small bifid robust setae along the anterior margin. The short ischium has setae on the anteroventral corner. The oblong merus bears bifid marginal robust setae on both margins; the carpus bears two rows of bifid robust setae. The propodus is slender and slightly curved, with two rows of marginal robust setae and setae posterodistally. The dactylus tapers to a sharply pointed tip, with small setae on both sides of the subapex. Pereopod 7 is elongate, 1.8 times as long as pereopod 5, and has a shallow, bilobed coxa. Article lengths from basis to dactylus are in the ratio 3.3: 1: 2.3: 1.7: 2.7: 1. The anterior margin of the basis has a row of bifid robust setae; its posterior margin bears long plumose setae bifid robust setae. The ischium is short and subrectangular. The elongate merus bears setae along both margins and one bifid robust seta posterodistally. The carpus is shorter and narrower than the merus, with several midlength setae along the anterior margin. The propodus is elongate, slender and slightly curved, bearing bifid robust setae along the anterior margin. The dactylus tapers to a pointed tip and has one thin setae 2/3 from the proximal end.

Pleon. Pleopods 1–3 are well developed. Their peduncles are cylindrical, longer than broad, fringed with several plumose setae, and bear a pair of retinaculae on the anterior margin. The inner ramus is slightly longer than the peduncle and has 9–10 articles; the outer ramus is shorter than the inner ramus, and both rami bear facial setae. Uropod 1 does not extend beyond the ends of the other uropods. Its peduncle is longer than either ramus, fringed with bifid robust setae, and has a posteroventral process at the apex. Both margins of both rami are lined with a row of robust setae; their distal margins are rounded and bear with several robust setae. Uropod 2 is slightly longer than uropod 3. Its peduncle is shorter than the inner and outer rami, and both with two bifid robust setae. The outer ramus is slightly longer than the inner one; both rami have a row of bifid robust setae and short and long robust setae on the distal margin. Uropod 3 is uniramous, with a peduncle much shorter than the ramus. The ramus is elongate and has a short second article; both outer and inner margins bear a row of long setae, and the apex has 4 long, stiff setae. The telson is subtrapezoidal and ends in a double-pointed apex, each point bearing one long robust seta and one short (thin) seta.

Female (allotype). Total body length is 3.9 mm (from tip of rostrum to apex of telson). (sexually dimorphic characters). Antenna 1 lacks an accessory flagellum, and its flagellum has 15 articles. Peduncular article 3 of antenna 2 bears 2 bifid robust setae at the ventrodistal corner. The inner plate of maxilla 2 lacks robust setae. Pereon. Gnathopod 1 is subchelate and smaller than that of the male. Its coxal plate is deeper than those of the male. The basis is more robust and 1.8 times as long as broad. The carpus is subtriangular, 1.5 times as long as broad, and has a setose posterior margin with the posterior distal margin produced into a short, stout tooth. The propodus is oval and shorter than the carpus; its palm is oblique and defined by a large bifid robust seta. The palmar margin has short setule, and the distal end is covered sparse plumose setae. The dactylus is curved and bears 3 short, stout robust setae on the inner margin. Gnathopod 2 resembles that of the male and is slightly smaller to gnathopod 1. The basis is slender, the carpus is 2.2 times as long as wide, and the propodus is wider than that of the male. Its palm is transverse and defined by 2 large bifid robust setae. The dactylus is curved, with fine setule and 5 short, stout robust setae on the grasping margin (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Remarks: Specimens of the new species Grandidierella halophilus were collected in a hypersaline habitat (~80 ppt) and were associated with seagrass (Ruppia maritima Linnaeus). To date, only two Grandidierella species, G. propodentata and G. exillis, have been reported from hypersaline environments. G. propodentata is notably similar to G. halophilus in having the unusual arborescent setae on the inner face of the outer lobe of the lower lip (Moore, 1986). Several differences from G. propodentata are also evident: (1) male antenna 2 article 4 is spout-like (vs. normal) (Moore, 1986); (2) the proximal tooth on the male gnathopod 1 propodus is directed inward (vs. posterior margin proximally concave, distally expanded; Moore, 1986); and (3) the male gnathopod 1 carpus is triangular, with two large, subequal teeth at the posterodistal corner (vs. posterodistal corner with produced tooth and posterior margin setose with a small tooth; Moore, 1986). Grandidierella halophilus differs from G. exillis by the presence of an accessory flagellum, arborescent setae on the inner face of the outer lobe of the lower lip, and a second article on the uropod 3 ramus. A sternal process in the male G. halophilus new species is seems to be unique among Grandidierella members. Only four species—G. bonnieroides, G. exillis, G. trispinosa, and G. spinicoxa—share this distinct character. Grandidierella halophilus resembles G. bonnieroides in having the male sternal process and a carpochelate gnathopod 1 with a produced tooth at the posterodistal corner, a produced small tooth on the inner face, and a small tooth on the setose posterior margin. In his investigations of material from the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico, Myers (1970) reported considerable population-level variation in the sternal process of G. bonnieroides, suggesting that most populations are genetically distinct. Consistent with Asari & Myers (1982), south Indian G. bonnieroides also exhibits distinct local variations, indicating the possibility of group sibling species. Grandidierella halophilus is readily distinguished from all other known species of the genus by the combination of: (1) coxal plate 2 with the ventral margin produced posteriorly into a triangular expansion; (2) uropod 3 peduncle inflated, with the ramus bearing a small second article; and (3) lower lip with arborescent setae on the inner face of the outer lobe. In addition, all robust setae on antennae 1–2, gnathopods 1–2, pereopods 5–7, and uropods 1–3 are bifid. This character has not been reported elsewhere in the genus, but is shown in illustrations for G. mahafalensis (Ruffo, 1958) and G. propodentata (Moore, 1986) (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2012)

Description: The coxal plate of gnathopod 1 is suboval and unproduced. Its basis is stout, 1.8 × as long as broad; the carpus is 1.5 times as long as broad, with the posterodistal corner extended into a tooth and the oblique inner face bearing two smaller teeth... Gnathopod 2 is subchelate, and its coxa is produced posteroventrally into a tooth. The basis is slender and not distally expanded. The carpus is longer than the propodus, 2.2 × as long as wide, with a crenulated posterior margin bearing pectinate setae (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).

Reference: Chilton (1925)

Diagnosis: The pleopod rami are about 0.9 × the length of the peduncle, and the uropod 3 ramus is about 0.6 × the length of the peduncle. The telson is apically incised, with 6–7 robust setae on each lobe (Lowry & Myers, 2022).
Reference: Lowry & Myers (2022)
Dexter (1996) PMBC Res. Bull. 61: 1–28

Description: Along the dorsal midline, the head is as long as pereonites 1–2 combined; the rostrum is slender and acutely pointed (Just, 2004).
Reference: Just J (2004)

Description: The head is as long as the first three pereonites combined and bears a single cuticle lens. The first antennae are positioned between the eyes... Articles 7 of gnathopods 1 and 2 are sharp, and articles 2–4 are broad. Pereopods 3–4 are similar in structure, with articles 2–4 much broader than article 7. Uropod 3 is subfoliaceous, with the outer and inner rami equal in length. The telson is cleft, with acute apices and one seta at each tip (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2009) Nat. Hist. J. Chulalongkorn Univ. 9(1): 69–83

Diagnosis: The second peduncular segment of antenna 2 is distinctly longer than the first; the head has a narrow anterodistal end; the posteroventral corner of pleonal epimeron 3 is quadrate; and article 2 of pereopod 7 has a posterior lobe (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009).
Description: The head bears a small rostrum and four eyes, with a cuticle lense in the lateral pair. The eye is bigger than in A. cyclops... Gnathopods 1 and 2 have a sharp article 7 and broad articles 2–4. Uropod 3 is subfoliaceous, with the outer and inner rami equal. The telson is cleft, with acute apices and one seta at each tip (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2009) — first record for Thai waters

Description: The head is free and not coalesced with peraeonite 1. The rostrum is present and short, and the eye is present. The body is laterally compressed. Coxae 1–4 are longer than broad and overlapping. Gnathopods 1 and 2 are subequal, and both are subchelate. Uropod 2 has a ventromedial spur, with the inner ramus subequal to the outer ramus. Uropod 3 has a short peduncle, and its outer ramus is longer than the peduncle. The outer ramus is 2-segmented. The telson is laminar, cleft, and longer than broad (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009; Chilton, 1925).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2009); Chilton (1925) Tale Sap

Description: The first antennae are shorter than the second, and the second antennae are longer than the body length. The mandible incisors are dentate, and lacinia mobilis are present on both sides. Coxae 1–4 overlap. Gnathopod 1 is subequal to gnathopod 2, and both gnathopods are subchelate. Pereopods 5–7 bear many rows of facial and marginal robust setae and feather-like setae. The rami of uropod 3 bear dense feather-like setae. The telson is laminar and cleft (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2009).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2009) Nat. Hist. J. Chulalongkorn Univ. 9(1)

Description: The head has a notch on its anteroventral margin. Gnathopod 2 is larger than gnathopod 1; its coxa has a notch on the posteroventral margin, the merus is produced posterodistally, and the propodus is distally expanded, with the posterior margin slightly excavated distally. The palm is transverse and bears a subrectangular distomedial elevation with 6 robust setae; the palmar margin has 2 robust setae. The dactylus is toothed along the mid-posterior margin. Pleonites 1–3 each have paired mid-dorsal teeth on the posterior margin. The peduncle of uropod 1 bears two rows of basofacial robust setae. The telson is deeply cleft, as long as broad, and has distally truncated lobes bearing 5 to 7 long apical robust setae (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Remarks: Parelasmopus siamensis sp. nov. differs from P. poorei in lacking robust setae on the posterodistal corner of gnathopod 1 (versus 2 such setae present); in having a distomedial elevation on the palm of gnathopod 2, whereas P. poorei has a posteroproximal elevation; and in having the basis of pereopod 7 bulging outward rather than sigmoid-shaped (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2013) Zootaxa 3693(4): 501–533

Description: The lateral cephalic lobes are truncate, and the anteroventral margin is moderately recessed. A small tooth is present at the anteroventral corner; the eyes are present and oval shaped. Gnathopod 1 is larger than gnathopod 2 and is subchelate. Its coxa is subrectangular, and its robust basis is 2 × as long as broad. The merus is produced posterodistally into a tooth. The carpus is shorter than the propodus, subtriangular, and produced posterodistally. The propodus is robust, with an oblique palm bearing a deep excavation and a subrectangular, serrated distomedial edge; the dactylus overlaps the palm (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng et al. (2013) Zootaxa 3693(4) — redescription

Diagnosis: Pereopod 3 has a clearly three-pronged form (trifurcate), which gives rise to the species epithet (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Description: The material was collected from a seagrass bed at Ao Thale Nok, Khanom District, Nakhon Si Thammarat Province. The original paper provides the full morphological description and illustrations (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Remarks: This is the first record of the genus Cheiriphotis from the South China Sea (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2012).
Reference: ZooKeys 187: 71–89

Diagnosis: The propodus of gnathopod 1 is elongate, while the palm of gnathopod 2 bears 6 teeth and has a rounded palmar corner (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Description: Body length is 5.1 mm, and the eyes are round. The accessory flagellum of antenna 1 has 6 articles; the gnathopod 2 propodus is 1.5× as long as wide; and the telson is longer than broad and cleft to more than 95% of its (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Remarks: This species is closest to M. serratipalma, but differs in the following features: the gnathopod 1 palm lacks a distinct defining palmar corner; the gnathopod 2 merus is not produced into a tooth; the propodus is subtriangular; the dactyli of pereopods 3–7 are smooth and curved; and the inner ramus of uropod 3 bears only 1 proximal seta (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Reference: ZooKeys 307

Diagnosis: The palm of gnathopod 2 bears 7 teeth, and its propodus is unusually elongate, measuring 2.7× the length of the carpus (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Description: Body length is 1.65 mm. Antenna 1 has a 16-articulate flagellum plus 1 rudimentary article. The outer ramus of uropod 3 is long and biarticulate; the telson is broader than long, deeply cleft, and has truncate apices (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Remarks: It differs from R. ana and R. lokoa by possessing eyes, whereas the other two are eyeless; the antenna 1 peduncle lacks robust setae; the gnathopod 2 propodus is longer; and the uropod 3 rami are shorter. This is the first record of the genus Rotomelita from the West Pacific (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2013).
Reference: ZooKeys 307

Diagnosis: The male gnathopod 2 distolateral crown bears 4 spines; the pleonite/urosomite formula is 7-7-7-5-6-2; and the dactylus of pereopods 5–7 has 2 accessory spines (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2014).
Description: The male holotype is 6.3 mm long. Antenna 1 has a 5-articulate accessory flagellum and a 16–25-articulate primary flagellum. The left mandible incisor is 3-dentate and the right is 4-dentate. The maxilla 1 inner plate bears 2 apical plumose setae. Male gnathopod 2 is sexually dimorphic, with the larger propodus bearing 4 rounded spines on its distolateral crown. Pereopods 6–7 have bunches of long, slender setae on the merus, carpus, and propodus. The uropod 3 inner ramus is scale-like, and the outer ramus is 2-articulate and more than 2× the peduncle length. The telson is deeply cleft, with lobes tapering to acute points (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2014).
Remarks: This species differs from D. cotesi, D. oahu, and D. tulear in having 4 spines rather than 3 on the male gnathopod 2 distolateral crown. It differs from D. pacifica in the poorly developed fourth spine, a gnathopod 1 carpus longer than the propodus, and 2 accessory spines on the pereopods 3–4 dactyli rather than 1 (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2014).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng, K., Pattaratumrong, M.S., Puttapreecha, R. (2014). Melitid amphipods from the Gulf of Thailand, with a description of Dulichiella pattaniensis, a new species. ZooKeys 408: 1–18. doi:10.3897/zookeys.408.7292

Authors: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Shin, M. (2018).
Diagnosis: As in the genus diagnosis, the right mandible incisor is 4-dentate and the left is 6-dentate; the maxilla 1 outer plate bears 6 apical robust setal-teeth, and the maxilla 1 palp is absent. The female gnathopod 1 coxa is large and strongly produced posterodistally, with a strongly obtuse palm (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2018).
Description: The male holotype is 6.6 mm. Antenna 1 has an 11-articulate flagellum lined with pappose setae, and antenna 2 has an 11-articulate flagellum. The maxilla 1 outer plate bears 6 terminal serrate setal-teeth, and its palp is absent; the maxilla 2 inner plate has an enlarged proximal seta. Male gnathopod 1 is weakly chelate, with a well-developed carpal lobe, while the gnathopod 2 propodal palm is smoothly concave and lined with pappose setae. Uropod 3 is uniramous, and the telson is cleft to half its length (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2018).
Remarks: Allorchestoides differs from Allorchestes in having a 1-articulate maxilla 1 palp that is reduced/tiny, whereas it is absent in Allorchestoides. It differs from Exhyalella in having a well-developed carpus with a posterior carpal lobe on male gnathopod 2 and a telson cleft to half-length, whereas the telson is entire in Exhyalella. Allorchestoides is the only dogielinotid genus known to live in brackish water, associated with submerged Nipa palm trunks (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2018).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Shin, M. (2018). Discovery of a new genus and species of dogielinotid amphipod (Crustacea: Amphipoda: Dogielinotidae) from the Nipa palm in Thailand, with an updated key to the genera. PLOS ONE 13(10): e0204299. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0204299

Diagnosis: The left mandible has a 5-dentate lacinia mobilis, and the palm of gnathopod 2 is approximately 33% of the posterior margin length. The uropod 3 peduncle bears 3 robust setae, while each telson lobe bears 4 robust setae (Suklom, Danaisawadi & Wongkamhaeng, 2021).
Description: The male body is 5.5 mm long, and the eyes are large (>1/3 head length). Antenna 2 has a 13-articulate flagellum. Gnathopod 1 has palmate lobes on the merus, carpus, and propodus, covered with palmate setae. Epimera 2 have 23 slits, epimera 3 have 16 slits, and uropod 3 is uniramous (Suklom, Danaisawadi & Wongkamhaeng, 2021).
Remarks: This is the third species of Floresorchestia recorded from Thailand and is clearly distinguishable from F. boonyanusithii and F. buraphana by multiple characters (see key table below) (Suklom, Danaisawadi & Wongkamhaeng, 2021).
Reference: Biodivers Data J. 9: e63197

Authors: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Sumitrakij, R., Keetapithchayakul, T.S. (2022)
Diagnosis: As in the genus diagnosis: uropod 1 has robust setae on the outer ramus, whereas the outer ramus of uropod 2 lacks robust setae; the basis of pereopod 7 has no posterodistal lobe; antenna 1 is long, extending from the midpoint to the end of peduncular article 5 of antenna 2; the eye is medium-sized (1/5–1/3 head length); gnathopod 1 is not sexually dimorphic, with a transverse palm and a dactylus shorter than the palm; gnathopod 2 is sexually dimorphic, subchelate in the male and mitten-shaped in the female (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2022).
Description: The male gnathopod 2 is mitten-shaped, with a slightly expanded basis. The merus, carpus, and propodus each bear a posterior lobe covered with palmate setae. The carpus is well-developed, and its posterior lobe projects between the merus and propodus. The propodus is twice as long as wide; its palm is obtuse and smooth, lacking a protuberance or shelf near the dactylar hinge, and the dactylus is shorter than the palm. The gill is lobate. The telson is longer than broad and apically incised, with the dorsal midline vestigial or absent; it bears only apical robust setae, with 2 robust setae per lobe (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2022).
Remarks: Thailandorchestia is assigned to Protorchestiidae based on the following characters: maxilliped palp article 2 lacks a distomedial lobe; article 4 is small and distinct; gnathopod 2 is subchelate; pereopods 3–7 are simplidactylate; the pereopod 4 dactylus is basidactylate; and the telson bears only apical robust setae or apical plus marginal robust setae, with 1–6 robust setae per lobe. The species is a driftwood hopper that lives inside mangrove roots and rotting logs and feeds on decaying wood (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2022).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Sumitrakij, R., Keetapithchayakul, T.S. (2022). Thailandorchestia rhizophila sp. nov., a new genus and species of driftwood hopper (Crustacea, Amphipoda, Protorchestiidae) from Thailand. ZooKeys 1099: 139–153. doi:10.3897/zookeys.1099.82949

Diagnosis: In the male, the propodus of gnathopod 1 is broad, with a length less than 1.5× its breadth. The merus and carpus of gnathopod 1 each bear a posterodistal tooth, and the anterodistal corner of the gnathopod 2 basis is produced into a distinct tooth (Myers, 1988).
Description: Dense brown pigment bands occur on pereon segments 2–7 and pleon segments 1–3. In the male, pereon segments 2–3 bear strong, acute sternal processes. The antenna 1 accessory flagellum is 4-articulate, with the terminal article rudimentary; article 2 of the maxilla 1 palp has 5 distal spines. The male gnathopod 1 carpus is enlarged and subovoid, 1.5× as long as broad; its propodus is 2/3 the carpus length, with a deeply excavated palm bearing a strong posterodistal tooth, which the stout dactylus slightly overlaps. The male gnathopod 2 basis is stout, and its carpus and propodus are subequal. Pereopods 5–7 have length ratios of 2:4:5. The uropod 3 rami are subequal and elongate; the outer ramus has a small second article, and both rami bear long terminal setae (Myers, 1988).
Remarks: Originally described as Lembos quadrimanus from southeast India, the species was later transferred to Bemlos (Myers, 1988).
