Myers (1974) erected the subspecies B. quadrimanus mozambicus from Tanzania/Kenya, based on a tooth on the merus and carpus of female gnathopod 1. Western Australian material matches East African material in this respect, as does material from Madagascar (Ledoyer, 1982). Sivaprakasam's (1970) original material is unique in lacking these teeth; they may have been overlooked.
Reference: Sivaprakasam, T.N. (1970). Lembos quadrimanus sp. nov. — original description; Myers, A.A. (1988). The genera Archaeobemlos n.gen., Bemlos Shoemaker, Protolembos Myers and Globosolembos Myers (Amphipoda, Aoridae, Aorinae) from Australia. Records of the Australian Museum 40(5): 265–332. doi:10.3853/j.0067-1975.40.1988.158

Diagnosis: Monoliropus hapipandi differs from all other Monoliropus species in having abdominal appendages reduced to a single seta, a bi-articulate mandibular palp (rather than tri-articulate in other species), and a unique projection on the penultimate article of the maxilliped palp (Guerra-García, 2004).
Remarks: Mayer (1903) erected the genus Monoliropus. M. hapipandi is the only species with reduced abdominal appendages and a bi-articulate mandibular palp (Guerra-García, 2004).
Reference: Guerra-García, J.M. (2004). Littoral Caprellidea (Crustacea, Amphipoda) from Phuket, Thailand.

Diagnosis: Eyes are small. The accessory flagellum of antenna 1 is pluriarticulate, with 5 articles; article 3 of the mandibular palp is rectilinear or clavate. The coxae are small and relatively short, with coxa 1 dilated and produced forward. In males, gnathopod 1 is subchelate, while gnathopod 2 is subchelate and greatly larger than gnathopod 1. The dactyli of pereopods 6–7 are elongate and falcate. Uropods 1–2 are biramous, with slightly subequal rami and a ventrodistal process on the peduncle; uropod 3 is uniramous, and the telson is entire (Giles, 1885).
Description: This is a polymorphic species: young specimens have a moderately well-developed inner ramus on uropod 3, which disappears in fully developed adults. The male gnathopod 2 changes from an oblique-palmed form bearing 3 large teeth to a transverse form bearing 4–5 small, irregular teeth. Article 3 of antenna 1 is shorter than article 1 or 2, and the accessory flagellum is tri-articulate (Giles, 1885).
Remarks: The species is easily distinguished from most others by the large teeth on the palms of gnathopods 1 and 2. It was originally described from the Bay of Bengal (Giles, 1885), and was later reported from Sri Lanka (Walker, 1904); its distribution is Indo-Pacific (Giles, 1885).
Reference: Giles, G.M. (1885). Natural history notes from H.M.'s Indian Marine Survey Steamer 'Investigator'... No. 2. Description of two new species of the amphipod genus Melita from Bay of Bengal. Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 54: 69–71.

Diagnosis: Mayer (1903) described the genus Triliropus in the Siboga Expedition monograph. Triliropus is closely related to Tritella but differs in lacking swimming setae on antenna 2 and in having vestigial abdominal appendages in the female (Mayer, 1903).
Reference: Mayer (1903) Siboga Exped. 34.

Diagnosis: Gnathopod 2 has a small tooth near the distal end of the carpus, and the propodus palm bears 3–4 large projections. Epimeron 1 has an anteroventral tuft of setae; epimeron 3 is sinuous and has a simple cusp; uropod 3 is elongate (Savigny, 1816).
Description: Originally described from the Mediterranean or Red Sea, the species was reported from Vietnam (Imbach, 1967), Taiwan, and Peninsular Malaysia (Savigny, 1816).
Remarks: A species complex is suspected; its occurrence in Taiwan suggests another species complex in Leucothoidae (Savigny, 1816).
Reference: Savigny, J.C. (1816).

Diagnosis: The rostrum is long and linguiform, and the accessory flagellum is absent. Article 2 of the maxilla 1 palp is stout and bears several short apical teeth. The outer plate of maxilla 2 is broader than the inner plate, and both plates have plumose setae along their margins. The lower lip lacks inner lobes, and article 2 of the mandible palp is long. Gnathopod 2 lacks a carpal lobe and has more slender carpus and propodus articles. Pereopods 3–4 each bear a pair of stout locking spines. The telson is cleft and lacks large apical spines (Othman & Morino, 2006).
Description: Originally described as Listriella longipalma from the Straits of Melaka, Malaysia, this species was later transferred to Idunella (Othman & Morino, 2006).
Remarks: The species belongs to the genus Idunella, family Liljeborgiidae, and is recorded from Thai waters (Othman & Morino, 2006).
Reference: Othman, B.H.R., Morino, H. (2006). Listriella longipalma sp. nov., a new amphipod species (Crustacea: Liljeborgiidae) from the Straits of Melaka, Malaysia. Zootaxa 1305: 21–32.

Diagnosis: This is a small species with a subocular notch on the head and subround eyes bearing clear ommatidia. The male gnathopod 2 propodus has a pit on the inner face of its posterior margin, into which the dactylus tip fits (Appadoo & Myers, 2003).
Description: The male is 3.5 mm long. The type locality is Bain Boeuf, Mauritius, and the species is known only from Mauritius (Appadoo & Myers, 2003).
Remarks: Appadoo & Myers (2003) described this as one of five new species from Mauritius. The genus Elasmopus is one of the most diverse melitid genera in the Indo-Pacific tropics (Appadoo & Myers, 2003).
Reference: Appadoo, C., Myers, A.A. (2003). The genus Elasmopus (Crustacea: Amphipoda: Melitidae) from Mauritius (Indian Ocean) with description of five new species. Records of the Australian Museum 55(1): 61–84.

Diagnosis: The eye lobe is large and projects antero-ventrally between the 1st and 2nd antennae. In the female, the eye is restricted to the lobe, whereas in the adult male it extends to the dorsum of the head. Gnathopods 1 and 2 are slender and similar; males and females are alike, and article 6 is not expanded in the male and has no defined palm. Article 4 does not project postero-distally, and article 5 is not expanded. The peduncle of uropod 1 bears an interramal spine approximately 1/4 the length of the rami. The rami of uropod 3 are flat and paddle-shaped, with the inner (dorsal) ramus asymmetrically truncate. The telson is deeply cleft, and its lobes are notched and bear large spines. The ventral margin of pleonal epimeron 3 is toothed, and the accessory flagellum has 2 articles (Hoek, 1889).
Description: Hoek (1889) originally described the genus Megaluropus, which is confined to the Old World.
Remarks: Megaluropus differs from Gibberosus spp., which have a postero-distally projecting lobe on article 4 and an expanded article 5 of gnathopod 2, and from Resupinus coloni, which lacks the interramal spine on the peduncle of uropod 1 and has a 1-article accessory flagellum (Hoek, 1889).

Diagnosis: The rostrum is short, pointed, and directed downward (Spence Bate & Westwood, 1863–1868).
Description: First described from Banff, Scotland, as Monoculodes longimanus and subsequently transferred to Perioculodes (Spence Bate & Westwood, 1863–1868).
Remarks: Synonyms are Perioculodes grubei Boeck, 1871 and P. longimanus longimanus Spence Bate & Westwood, 1868. Its distribution is Atlanto-Mediterranean, with additional records from Kuwait, Cyprus, and Thai waters (Spence Bate & Westwood, 1863–1868).
Reference: Spence Bate, C., Westwood, J.O. (1863–1868). A history of the British sessile-eyed Crustacea.

Diagnosis: The head is 3/4 eye length, and its lobe is produced into a rounded lobe that is distally subacute. Mandibular palp article 3 is present; the maxilliped inner plate is expanded, and maxilliped palp article 2 does not extend beyond the merus. Pleonite 3 and urosomite 1 each have a notched dorsal margin. The uropod 3 inner ramus is narrowly rounded (Lowry & Stoddart, 2002).
Description: Described from Phuket Island, Thailand, in the Andaman Sea, at a depth of 32–61 m (Lowry & Stoddart, 2002).
Remarks: This is one of two Lepidepecreum species described from the Andaman Sea by Lowry & Stoddart (2002); it was compared with L. andamanensis in the same paper.
Reference: Lowry, J.K., Stoddart, H.E. (2002). The Lysianassoid Amphipod Genera Lepidepecreoides and Lepidepecreum in Southern Waters (Crustacea: Lysianassidae: Tryphosinae). Records of the Australian Museum 54(3): 335–364.

Diagnosis: The left mandible has a 4-dentate lacinia mobilis. In the male, gnathopod 1 has a palmate lobe on the merus, carpus, and propodus, each covered with palmate setae; the palm of gnathopod 2 extends along 31–35% of the posterior margin. The inner ramus of uropod 1 bears 4 marginal robust setae. The peduncle of uropod 3 bears 2 robust setae, and its rami lack marginal setae. Epimera 2 and 3 have 27 and 20 slits, respectively; each telson lobe bears 4 robust setae (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2016).
Remarks: This is one of two Floresorchestia species described as new in 2016, the other being F. buraphana (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2016).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Pattaratumrong, M.S. (2016). Two new species of Floresorchestia (Crustacea, Amphipoda, Talitridae) in Thailand. ZooKeys 635: 31–51.

Diagnosis: The left mandible has a 5-dentate lacinia mobilis. In male gnathopod 1, the merus, carpus, and propodus each bear a palmate lobe covered with palmate setae. In male gnathopod 2, the palm extends along 36–40% of the posterior margin. The inner ramus of uropod 1 has 3 marginal robust setae. The peduncle of uropod 3 bears 2 robust setae, and its rami lack marginal setae. Epimera 2 and 3 have 25 and 15 slits, respectively. Each telson lobe has 5 robust setae (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2016).
Remarks: This is one of two new Floresorchestia species described in 2016, along with F. boonyanusithii (Wongkamhaeng et al., 2016).
Reference: Wongkamhaeng, K., Dumrongrojwattana, P., Pattaratumrong, M.S. (2016). Two new species of Floresorchestia (Crustacea, Amphipoda, Talitridae) in Thailand. ZooKeys 635: 31–51.

Diagnosis: Antenna 1 peduncular article 1 is subequal in length to article 2, which is not geniculate. The posterior margins of the bases of pereopods 5–7 are strongly crenate. Pleonites 1–2 each have a small dorsodistal spine. The inner ramus of uropod 3 is minute (Lowry & Watson, 2002).
Description: Female holotype, 3.8 mm. Head with obtuse lateral cephalic lobes; anteroventral margin excavate and deeply notched; eyes apparently absent. Antenna 1 is longer than antenna 2; accessory flagellum 3-articulate; primary flagellum 16-articulate. Antenna 2 flagellum 9-articulate. Mandibular palp article 3 is approximately 0.6 times the length of article 2 and distally falcate. Gnathopod 1 subchelate; carpus approximately 2.8 times as long as wide and 1.5 times the length of the propodus; palm transverse. Gnathopod 2 subchelate and slightly larger than gnathopod 1; carpus without a posterior lobe; propodus approximately 2.5 times as long as wide; palm acute and slightly convex. Pereopods slender, with long, slender dactyli; bases of pereopods 5–7 strongly crenate posteriorly. Uropod 3 biramous; inner ramus scale-like and without distal setae; outer ramus approximately four times the length of the inner ramus and twice the length of the peduncle, 2-articulate. Telson deeply cleft, broader than long, with approximately four distal setae on each lobe. “Key to Species of the Gammarellid Group,” p. 204 (Lowry & Watson, 2002).
Remarks: Lowry & Watson considered N. kata most similar to N. merringannee from southern Australia. They distinguished N. kata by its slender pereopods, particularly the long, slender dactyli, and by the very short inner ramus of uropod 3 relative to the outer ramus. Because no male specimens were available, sexually dimorphic characters of male gnathopod 2 could not be documented (Lowry & Watson, 2002).
Reference: Lowry, J. & Watson, M. (2002). Revision of the gammarellid group, with a new species from the Andaman Sea (Crustacea, Amphipoda, Melitidae). Phuket Marine Biological Center Special Publication 23(1): 197–212.
